关系中金钱问题
    -  明确 “救急不救穷”，  与 “借出即送出”

    - 把丑话说在前面 - 契约精神保护感情
          +   白纸黑字写清金额，期限和还款
          +   事实往往是 因为不谈钱，最后才彻底伤了感情

    -  健康的资金往来
          +    借钱或合伙时， 彼此将对方视为具有独立财务风险和边界的个体

    - 混淆了 “价值” 与 “感情”
         +  你把“我对金钱边界的维护”误当成了“我对这段感情的否定”  
         +  “健康的、清晰的财务边界，恰恰是保护感情最好的防腐剂。”

Sales is about people and it’s about problem solving
    - People buy 4 things only:  time, money, sex, and approval/peace of mind
         +  time: 買 效率 與 勞動力外包

         +  money:  買 回報， 財富增長 或 風險規避

         + sex:   買吸引力 -  繁殖慾望， 吸引異性

         +  approval/peace of mind:  買 社交地位 與 心理安全感
              - 認可
              -  心理安全感： 買 的是 “晚上能睡得安穩” 的安心感

    - people buy aspirin always. Sell aspirin.

    - people buy from their friends.   Make everything else equal
         +  在理性邏輯無法分出勝負的關鍵時刻，決策權會交給感性
         +   將「交易」轉為「關係」 
         +   透過提供洞察、協助對方解決痛點、展現真誠的利他精神，建立超越一般買賣關係的信任感

    - Being valuable and useful is all you ever need to do to sell things.
         +  help people out.  Send interesting posts. 
              Write birthday cards. Record videos sharing your ideas for growing their business.
              Introduce people who would benefit from knowing each other then getting out of the way,
              expecting nothing in return.

body:
心態： 不卑不亢，大方自信
    - 創業者/晚輩
          + 乾淨利落， 頭髮清爽， 精神飽滿

          + 目標明確： 開拓高價值事業，止損無效的情感投資

    - 把 amos 看作 導師/投資人
         + 尊重大佬，展現項目價值， 尋找伯樂的機遇

    -   放下女方， 止損

    -  對 host 保持禮貌與距離 

    -   談投資
          + 表現出「我這是一個優質的投資機會，我想邀請您作為第一波合夥人」

          +   “Amos，上次您說願意幫忙，我心裡一直很感激。

我最近在做一個 AI 知識自動化的項目，想請教您的看法，順便問問您有沒有興趣做投資人？

其實我更想聽聽您的商業建議，或者您覺得我該先準備些什麼？”

                 -  表現積極 - “太好了， 那下週找個你方便時間，我請你喝咖啡，詳細跟你匯報”
                 -  含蓄 - “如果不方便沒關係，沒問題，也就隨口跟您請教一下。”

        +  商業pitch
                -  我看到一個問題： 傳統行業最怕人離職、經驗歸零；
                個人也常被鎖事淹沒；

                   其實我想我想用 AI 做一個『超級助理』，把經驗和瑣事自動化沉澱下來，
                 做到真正的知識複利 - 讓經驗越滾越大、變成你的超級助理。
                    目前已經有了一個雛形， 以你看這方向在市場上到底有沒有前景？

               -  像傳統行業最怕人離職、經驗流失；
              對個人來說，也需要一個超級助理幫忙整理資料和處理雜務。 
             我就是想把這個『知識複利』和『自動代理』做出來，讓經驗和時間都能自動幫人滾雪球。

                - 個人或初創公司的 知識複利 和 自主代理營運
                     +  傳統行業 比如 醫療，金融， 律所，工程師 最值錢的是 “人的經驗”， 但人一離職或一忙碌，經驗就流失
                     +  個人 知識複利 - 相當於私人助理， 比如自己的閱讀，文檔整合，
                     +   個人自主代理 -  處理生活中繁瑣的“低價值營運。 比如 自動整理每週代辦事項

                -  人的經驗和過往案例全部散落在腦子裡，文檔裡，沒有辦法做到“知識複利”
                    + 專業領域的知識自動化。 把個人或團隊過往的案例，文檔和經驗融合起來，打造一個專屬的知識庫；
                   更進一步，它能直接進行 “自主代理營運”， 把哪些重複，繁瑣的低價工作自動化處理

               -   私有數據與知識複利：  內部所有文檔和案例， 融合成一個專屬資料庫。
                    當新人進來或遇到老問題， 系統會立刻調用過往成功經驗給出精準答案， 讓經驗留下來

                    +   自主代理營運：  設定好工作流後， 這個系統可以主動幫助處理那些重複的日常： 比如基本條款，
                    把團隊從這些繁瑣的 低價值動作 解放出來，去專注真正核心的事情上

               -  目前mvp 已經在跑這個邏輯。  想聽聽你的看法 - 以你的經驗，你覺得在實際上， 像這樣的小團隊或專業人士，最願意為 什麽樣的效率提升 買單？

Title: #insight
---

Reasonable > Rational 
   - Rational（理性）關乎邏輯、算力與效率（How to optimize）

   - Reasonable（合情合理）關乎情境、價值、永續性與共情（What is right or acceptable in reality）

   - “先緩後剛”的 溝通節奏
        -  先接納：   無論對方多麽不理性， 先說一句 “我明白你的考慮”

        -  再陳述：  將你的rational 需求轉化爲對方的利益

        -  終妥協：  在不觸碰核心底線的前提下， 給出一個“雙方可接受的解”  
            +   內心rational (冷靜分析局勢）， 外表展現  reasonable (給人面子與空間）

body:
無所謂

    -  

---
Title: #softskills
---

鬆弛感溝通

    -   面對前輩或有一定社交距離的對象時， 學會
   “把具體執行的壓力扛在自己身上，把選擇的舒適度留給對方”
         +   少用 邏輯審判 （少說 ‘你之前說過’) 

         +    用“自身時間盲區” 作為自然的切入點
               -   把 “需要對方配合” 包裝成 “自己時間有點亂，需要提前規劃”，
                將主導權交給對方， 同時順理成章地拋出時間

    -  拿捏 “主導權” 與 “尊重感” 的平衡
         +    分佈推進：  把最核心 的定下來 （建立共識）
         +    把其他 或 細節 交給自己去後台運籌帷幄 （展現 擔當與細心）

         +    把繁瑣的篩選工作留給自己， 展現專業與貼心

    -  動態戰術轉換 ：  從 被動防守 到 “主動佈局”

         +     不以一時的冷熱來判斷關係， 而是用 “高價值的行為” 去破局

   -  讓對方覺得 “這件事是他自己決定的”， 而不是 “被你推著走的”
         +   以我為主， 以客為尊的句型
         +    多用 “我想請教 …”,  “這週剛好有空 …”, “你看怎樣方便 …”

動態主導， 而不是 被動跟隨
    -  潛意識 “擔心主動提要求 會被拒絕， 或者 害怕給對方添麻煩

    -   主導權 不等於 ”強勢命令“， 而是 ” 承擔起幫雙方做決策的責任“
         +    當你說出“ 時間我來定，地點我來找，你只要人來就好”，
         其實是把最繁瑣的 決策成本 扛在自己身上， 把最舒適的體驗留給對方。
          這不是被動， 這叫 “以退為進的紳士主導權”

         +   利益保護：
               永遠記住： 在追求合作的過程中， 你是帶著“價值” 去尋求共贏的，
               而不是去乞求施捨。 當你確立了這個底氣， 你的姿態就會自然地從 “求全” 變成 “對等”

你在尋找怎樣的連結？
    - 這次出門， 是為了滋養自己， 還是為了逃避孤獨？

    -  停止用“社交” 來 治療 “孤獨”
        +   帶著 放鬆的 願望去，卻掉進了一個 “被要求付出”的場域

        +   真正的解藥 是  高質量的深度連結： 真正懂你，舒服的個體交流，或者在大自然中獨處

當有僵硬感時， 問自己 ”此刻，我的身體在幫我防禦什麼？ 我在害怕展現出怎樣的自己？“

對”關係中的對等於尊重“ 有很高的要求
    - 當感受到別人用功利，索取的眼光 來對待你的付出， 你會迅速啟動防禦並感到被冒犯

    -  邊界訊號：  開始清楚自己不喜歡怎樣的交換關係

   -   建立 “健康的自私” 與 邊界

              -    如果這段關係本來就是 消耗性的，  學會在第一時間果斷拒絕，而不是 用 “做好人” 來勉強自己

                   +    把 “你的價值”  和 “對方的反應” 切割開， 別人的態度就再也傷不到你

        +    挑選 真正對等，滋養的場域
              -  去和 那些 懂得感恩，懂得互相尊重，能量乾淨的人 交往

強烈不舒服是在保護你的核心價值觀
    -  你不想成為那種用 金錢或 物質來定義自己價值的人

       +    價值感的防禦 
              -   在用 “道德鄙視” 來保護自己免受 “金錢焦慮恐懼”的傷害
              -   心裡防衛

    -   賺錢能力  與 做人價值 徹底解綁  
        +    賺錢能力 只是 一種商業能力 和 選擇 的結果， 絕對不等於你這個人的靈魂價值

        +     你可以一邊追求財務自由， 一邊打心底裡鄙視那些 把人命價值的拜金價值觀

    -   承認 “我希望自己更有錢” 並不是一件羞恥的事
        +     不再用“清高” 去壓抑自己對財務安全的渴望，你就能更客觀地去處理自己的工作與投資 

    -    對那些不同頻的人， 冷漠是最好的溫柔
        +     這不是同一條路上的人
        +     把注意力轉回你真正關心的人事物上

 如何在“金錢社會” 中活出你
    -    分清 “生存的規則”  與 “存在的價值”
         +   謀生：  在社會層面， 確實需要學會玩這個遊戲， 這是對現實的理性應對

         +   我是誰： 在精神層面， 必須在心裡為自己劃出一塊“免於被標價”的自留地。
               賺錢只是一種生存工具， 它絕對不能成為定義你靈魂價值的標準

   -    看清社交場域的 “遊戲規則”
         +    既然知道它是個名利場，  就不要對它抱有 “能找到真誠連結”的期待
         +    帶著 ”我來應酬一下“的旁觀者心態去， 用最禮貌最冷漠的社交面具應對即可

    - 把能量投回真正滋養你的”非金錢世界“
         +   金錢社會給予你的疲憊， 需要用”非功利的事物“ 來治療

amos 身份切換：  潛在商業導師/投資人
    -   專業，理性， 不要帶入任何情感抱怨或 顯得急切

心態： 穩固關係、收獲經驗、測試邊界

    - 請教 商業智慧 為主

    - 不卑不亢， 把姿態放低去聽他講商業經驗， 對話真誠

    - 談事情直奔主題、有方案就直接提出、不卑不亢

    -  把焦點放在你的事業與項目上：  尋求投資或商業指導的創業者

    -  對hiking活動 - 客觀， 成熟， 大器
        +   “ 對我來說，學習了一些和不同人打交道的經驗。
           而且也去了不同的地方，對香港的歷史和人文有了更深入的了解。 
           不過說實話，在這個過程中，我也看到了自己的一些侷限，比如有時候有些被動，覺得怕過界、怕尷尬“

    -  絕對不要提及情感糾葛

談話推薦

    -  建立專業共識與尊重
        +   表達感謝他抽出時間， 並肯定他過去載房地產界或商業上給予你的啟發與“朋友”情誼

              -   “這幾年一起行山，看你處理事情，都學到很多的”
                   “對我來說，學習了一些和不同人打交道的經驗。
           而且也去了不同的地方，對香港的歷史和人文有了更深入的了解。 
           不過說實話，在這個過程中，我也看到了自己的一些侷限，比如有時候有些被動，覺得怕過界、怕尷尬； 
              我以前做事 總覺得什麼想靠自己扛   “

    -   商業導師 -  請教大局觀 和 實戰經驗
        +   “不過我在想， 自己以前太侷限在技術裡。 像你過去在商業和地產經歷過那麼多風浪，視野完全不一樣”

               -  商業請益 - 談 判斷標準
                   +   “我最近在看一些新方向， 但總覺得自己缺乏大局觀。  特別是現在大環境變化這麼快。
                          像你以前看個項目，或者決定投入的時候， 最核心的標準是什麼？  你通常會看重 “人”的哪些特質？”

                   +   當聊 如何評估項目，如何看人，如何做資源槓桿時，對方可能會主動提起 
                        “你現在手頭在做什麼項目？ 卻不缺資金或支持”

               -  幫 傳統行業或個人 解決效率問題的工具
                    +  “是變化太快。 所以我現在做這個自動化， 是從個人日常工作中遇到什麼痛點，覺得什麼地方浪費時間，
                     就去幫忙省時間，提高效率”

                    +   “比如在健康方面， 健康飲食 或 醫療管理資訊很繁雜， 如果能用自動化 把這些複雜的營養，
                           健康知識整理   成 簡單可執行的日常方案， 就挺有價值的”

                     +  “用在跟健康管理相關的地方？  比如幫老年人 或家裡人 自動梳理醫療數據，
                           或是把複雜的健康報告轉化爲淺顯易懂的日常建議；  或者 飲食營養數據等”

                     +   “其實 跟你以前項目或房產管理差不多 -  就是看什麼地方流程繁瑣，資訊不對稱。 
                           我做這個方向，是想看能不能 幫一些傳統的小團隊或個人把繁瑣的流程自動化，省下時間做更有價值的事”

                     +    “您覺得現在這個年代，如果想從小生意做起、去幫別人解決甚麼樣的痛點，最容易跑出商業價值？”

                - 務實
                     +   “ 我現在做這個自動化項目，其實本金也不多，也就是拿自己有限的資源在做。 
                          從最小的痛點開始做一些能實際效果的東西“

                -  試探， 看他願不願意 給予 “實質支持”
                     +   “雖然技術沒問題，但在資源和商業上，我自己資金有限。 
                            今天見你， 也是想聽聽你的看法 -  像你當年的早期項目，
                           如果是我這種階段，你覺得值不值的找一兩個洞商業的前輩來做天使投資，或者你覺得我應該怎麼做”
                             -  “明白，我也就是自己先摸索，今天主要是來聽您指點的”

                    +    “ 如果你顧慮風險。 我現在需要的只是一筆很小的天使啟動金， 用來把這個工具推給第一批客戶。
                        如果有現金流都可以按比例分紅”

                - 人生智慧
                     +   “你當年在我們這個年紀， 是怎麼看  什麼才是最重要的”

      +    AI 股票
               - nvda, googl 

    -   切入商業項目 - 「客觀分析項目瓶頸、渴望高效推進」的姿態說出來時
         +   簡述 你的項目 
               -  “你覺得現在這個大環境， 像我們這個年紀想做企業或賺錢，應該抓什麼？”

        +   簡明 介紹你目前正在開發的項目 （突出 痛點， 技術壁壘或市場潛力），
              展現你在技術執行力的專業 （比如你對 架構與產品的掌控）

        +   “我做這個方向， 產品雛形已經跑通。 現在最大的瓶頸不是技術， 而是要把資源配置。
              說實話，如果這個階段 能有 懂行的前輩 在資金上給予支持，會穩很多”

   -    尋求具體指導與資源
        +    以 “尋求商業導師 mentor” 的姿態請教他對你項目的看法：
               “Amos, 你在市場經歷豐富，我想聽聽你以投資人的角度，怎麼看這個項目的商業模式和落地風險？”

        +   觀察他是否主動重提 “願意幫忙”的承諾。 
             如果他主動提及， 再進一步談具體的合作架構 （ 如顧問，資源對接或天使投資）

女生溝通不足 （不具備成熟維繫關係的意願或能力）

host (資訊操縱，圈子排擠或利益綁定）， 被動陷入一個由他人主導的社交戲碼中

Title: #insight
---

If you're a good person, you should try to date people who are good judges of character, because they have fewer options. 

They're prevented from dating all the various kinds of bad people, because they can see how bad they are.
    - 去追求那些选项少、但眼光极高的人

底層價值觀
    -  誠信 與 責任感   Accountability & Integrity
        +   出了問題， 習慣說 “我們怎麼解決”， 而不是 甩鍋或指責 （拒絕受害者心態）
        +    承諾過的事會放在心上； 如果做不到，會提前溝通
        +     對自己的情緒和行為負責， 不把伴侶或朋友當作情緒宣洩的垃圾桶

   - 情緒成熟度 與 內省能力  Emotional Maturity & self-reflection 
        +    跳出 “對錯輸贏”的 執念， 在衝突時更關注 “關係的連接”
        +     具備自我覺察能力， 願意承認自己的盲區或錯誤，並有成長型思維 （願意為更好的自己和關係調整）
        +      能夠承受不確定性和壓力， 而不是在關係遇到挫折時就立刻逃避或採取攻擊姿態

    - 對邊界與自主性的尊重  Respect for boundaries & Autonomy
        +   懂得 “愛不是佔有”；  尊重對方是一個獨立的個體， 有自己的社交圈，隱私和空間， 不會要求黏腻或全盘掌控
        +    不會試圖去“改造”或“拯救”對方， 而是接受真實的對方， 並在此基礎上共同成長

    -  善良與共情底線 Empathy & Moral Baseline

自主權 是你的心理安全島

成年人世界往往充滿了 微觀政治
    -  社交時習慣性地尋找 權力對比

拯救者情結 與  過度防禦  的拉鋸

你無意中散發 “高能量穩定感” 成為了吸鐵石

設立 “責任防火牆” ： 分清 “我的課題” 與 “對方的課題”
    -  當別人想把問題和責任推給你時，心理默念 “這是他的課題，不是我的”

    -   可以給予同理，但絕對不接過對方的方向盤
         +    “聽到你遇到這事挺不容易的” 
         +    “那你打算怎麼處理？”   <- 把解決問題的權力和責任，原封不動地還給對方

    -  允許關係停在“舒適的平視區”
          +     當發現有人試圖掌控你 或依賴你時， 只需要降低這段關係的熱度
          +    用禮貌，客套的態度， 將關係溫和地拉回到安全的“平時”  

   -   允許自己偶爾表現不好接近
          +     你的價值從來不需要通過 “幫別人收拾攤子” 來證明

區分  “理性的價值交換” vs  “臣服於權力”
    -   在成熟的社會， 合作 是基於 利益與價值的平等交換
         +      求助或合作 是一場 “各取所需”的 成年人協作， 並不等於 交出主導權

    - 重新定義 “求助”：  從“示弱” 到 “調動資源”
         +     向有經驗，有資源的上位者請教或尋求合作， 看作是 “招募你的商業/人生合夥人”，
          而不是 “向權威低頭”。   對方只是提供工具或橋樑的人。 
                 -   你可以用你的專業與價值去跟他們交換，而不是靠出賣尊嚴

         +     允許合作， 但守住邊界
                 -  心理練習   “ 我可以借用對方的平台或資金/機遇，但我內心的底線和決定權依然在我自己手裡”
                 -   保持合作的彈性，同時用我們前面提到的“責任防火牆” 守住自己的核心利益

         +     接納 “不完美的現實世界”
                 -   真正的成熟，是看清了這個世界的功利與規則之後，依然願意帶著智慧去利用規則，而不是賭氣把自己孤立起來

---
Title: #self
---

精英主义 同平民主义

平民等於善良， 精英等於勢利
    - 傾向於用 群體標籤 來定義 個人的 品格
        +    忽視了 個體的多樣性
        +     無論哪個階層， 都有真誠善良的人，也有利己和勢利的人

    -  同情心的“救贖”
        +    在他們身上看到了過去的自己或父母的影子。 
               去幫助或同情他們， 某種程度上 是在 治癒內心深處那個曾經感到自卑或脆弱的自己。
        +    讓你 陷入 “拯救者心態”， 忽略了 現實中 人際互動的複雜性和邊界感

    -   防禦性的道德優越

    -   稀缺心態帶來的防禦

    -   真正的精英 擁有 “情緒與資源的餘裕”
         +  正站穩腳跟、有實力的人，往往擁有心理與物質的餘裕（Abundance Mindset）；
     他們不需要透過剝削別人、佔小便宜或貶低他人來證明自己的價值

    -  人品無關階級
         +   你的「創傷」來自於特定的人，而不是整個階層
         +   剝離了「平民 vs 精英」的意識形態濾鏡後，你看世界的眼光變得更立體了

         +   用「對方的行為模式、邊界感與人品」去評估一個人，而不是用他的出身背景來貼標籤

整合與彈性
    -   將 “道德評價“ 從 ”社會階層“ 中剝離
         +     人的品格（善良，真誠，自私，勢利） 是個人的選擇和性格特質，與有錢，學歷或階層無必然關係。
                 看人時， 直接看這個個體的行為本身

    -   接納父親的侷限，完成心理上的”分化“
         +      對父親保持理解與感恩，同時允許自己發展處更適應力的智慧 - 這不是虛偽，而是成熟

    -    轉化 同情心 為 ”慈悲與邊界“
         +     健康同理心需要伴隨邊界感。
                香港是一個高度現實但規則清晰的社會， 學會在保護自己的前提下與各階層的人交往，
                欣賞不同背景之人的優點， 同時不對任何人抱有過度的道德幻想（無論是窮人還是精英）

    -  接鏡母親的”開朗與學習新事物“

潛意識背後
    - 在你成長的早期，沒有獲得足夠多的“無條件的熱情與肯定”；
      內心深處那個渴望被接納，被看見的“內在小孩” 便發揮作用。
      此時，任何主動釋放熱情的人，對你都具有致命吸引力。
      你被吸引的， 是那種“被熱烈接納”的感覺

    -  你太渴望溫暖，以至於選擇性地忽略了試探，利益計算或邊界模糊

   -  分不清 “情感上的熱烈” 與 “人際間的邊界”
       +    將對方的外在表現（熱情，歡迎） 等同於 他們的 內在品格 （真誠，善良）
             +  在現代商業，熱情往往是一種習得的“社交工具” 或 “職業技能”， 而不是 情感的流露

    -   勢利 -  有價值就貼上來； 一旦無利可圖， 立刻不認人
       +    保持安全距離。  不投入真感情， 不感到憤怒， 也不必自我懷疑。

    -  合理邊界

   -   允许自己偶尔表现不好接近
          +     你的价值从来不需要通过 “帮别人收拾摊子” 来证明

区分  “理性的价值交换” vs  “臣服于权力”
    -   在成熟的社会， 合作 是基于 利益与价值的平等交换
         +      求助或合作 是一场 “各取所需”的 成年人协作， 并不等于 交出主导权

    - 重新定义 “求助”：  从“示弱” 到 “调动资源”
         +     向有经验，有资源的上位者请教或寻求合作， 看作是 “招募你的商业/人生合伙人”，

         +     允许合作， 但守住边界
                 -  心理练习   “ 我可以借用对方的平台或资金/机遇，但我内心的底线和决定权依然在我自己手里”
                 -   保持合作的弹性，同时用我们前面提到的“责任防火墙” 守住自己的核心利益

         +     接纳 “不完美的现实世界”
                 -   真正的成熟，是看清了这个世界的功利与规则之后，依然愿意带著智慧去利用规则，而不是赌气把自己孤立起来

精英主义 同平民主义

平民等于善良， 精英等于势利
    - 倾向于用 群体标签 来定义 个人的 品格
        +    忽视了 个体的多样性
        +     无论哪个阶层， 都有真诚善良的人，也有利己和势利的人

    -  同情心的“救赎”
        +    在他们身上看到了过去的自己或父母的影子。 
               去帮助或同情他们， 某种程度上 是在 治愈内心深处那个曾经感到自卑或脆弱的自己。
        +    让你 陷入 “拯救者心态”， 忽略了 现实中 人际互动的复杂性和边界感

    -   防御性的道德优越

    -   稀缺心态带来的防御

    -   真正的精英 拥有 “情绪与资源的余裕”
         +  正站稳脚跟、有实力的人，往往拥有心理与物质的余裕（Abundance Mindset）；
     他们不需要透过剥削别人、占小便宜或贬低他人来证明自己的价值

    -  人品无关阶级
         +   你的「创伤」来自于特定的人，而不是整个阶层
         +   剥离了「平民 vs 精英」的意识形态滤镜后，你看世界的眼光变得更立体了

         +   用「对方的行为模式、边界感与人品」去评估一个人，而不是用他的出身背景来贴标签

整合与弹性
    -   将 “道德评价“ 从 ”社会阶层“ 中剥离
         +     人的品格（善良，真诚，自私，势利） 是个人的选择和性格特质，与有钱，学历或阶层无必然关系。
                 看人时， 直接看这个个体的行为本身

    -   接纳父亲的局限，完成心理上的”分化“
         +      对父亲保持理解与感恩，同时允许自己发展处更适应力的智慧 - 这不是虚伪，而是成熟

    -    转化 同情心 为 ”慈悲与边界“
         +     健康同理心需要伴随边界感。
                香港是一个高度现实但规则清晰的社会， 学会在保护自己的前提下与各阶层的人交往，
                欣赏不同背景之人的优点， 同时不对任何人抱有过度的道德幻想（无论是穷人还是精英）

    -  接镜母亲的”开朗与学习新事物“

潜意识背后
    - 在你成长的早期，没有获得足够多的“无条件的热情与肯定”；
      内心深处那个渴望被接纳，被看见的“内在小孩” 便发挥作用。
      此时，任何主动释放热情的人，对你都具有致命吸引力。
      你被吸引的， 是那种“被热烈接纳”的感觉

    -  你太渴望温暖，以至于选择性地忽略了试探，利益计算或边界模糊

   -  分不清 “情感上的热烈” 与 “人际间的边界”
       +    将对方的外在表现（热情，欢迎） 等同于 他们的 内在品格 （真诚，善良）
             +  在现代商业，热情往往是一种习得的“社交工具” 或 “职业技能”， 而不是 情感的流露

    -   势利 -  有价值就贴上来； 一旦无利可图， 立刻不认人
       +    保持安全距离。  不投入真感情， 不感到愤怒， 也不必自我怀疑。 
              这知识对方的生存策略，与你的价值无关

    -  合理边界 
       +     大家精力有限， 对不同的人 投入不同的时间与注意力， 是一种 自我能量管理

       +     接受这种 “不完美但健康的疏离”， 不强求

   -  保护自己 不要靠 冷酷无情， 只需要靠 清晰的边界

       +    把你的精力 和 情感 当作宝贵的资产
              -   对于功利型的人：   只进行最低限度的互动， 公事公办，绝不透支信任
              -   对于成熟社交的人：  接受舒适感，不追求每个人都成为挚友
              -   对于真正 真诚的人： 把你的真诚留给他们，建立深度，滋养彼此的关系

       +    与过去和解： 带有锋芒的善意
              -   保留父亲传给你的 善良和温暖，这是你最珍贵的底色
              -   为这份善良披上一层现代的盔甲 -  带有锋芒的善意。 
              -    善良是你的选择， 而边界是你的保护

       +   带有锋芒的善意
             -     带著觉察去互动， 给自己三秒钟的暂停  
                   +    允许自己 “先冷静， 后回应”

             -    温和的语气 +  坚定的边界 = 完美的锋芒
                   +    可以面带微笑，语气温和，但立场坚定地说“不” 或“ 这对我不太方便”

             -    将精力给“值得的人”
                   +     对于 过度功利的人， 用礼貌，疏离和程序化的态度应对 - 不报复，不纠缠， 不内耗

调整自己的心态与行动
     -  打破旧有的“心里忠诚”：
   追求更好的生活，学习更高的格局，不是背叛，而是自我成长的自然延伸

     - 靠近 滋养你的“成长磁场”， 远离 消耗你的 “贫穷心态” 
          +   无论对方背景如何， 只要对方 “抱怨，占便宜，榨取”， 果断拉开距离

     -   你的专业，你的清醒觉察，你的独立思考，是你立足的底气

发型
    - 希望兩側收乾淨（Fade），頂部能剪出層次感 (Texturizing/打薄層次) 以便於抓出蓬鬆感
        +  兩側 Fade
        +  露出眉型，清爽的前額與眉型呼應  
        +  頂部蓬鬆，增加頂部高度

    - 吹風技巧
        +  吹風時逆著髮性逆向吹掠，並用手或捲梳將髮根向上提拉。
        +  冷風定型： 熱風吹出造型後，切換至冷風吹 5 秒定型，利用熱脹冷縮原理鎖定髮根立體度。

    - 光髮蠟（Matte Paste/Clay），它能增加頭髮的質感與厚度
        +  少量、均勻、避開頭
        +   讓髮泥沾附在頭髮的中後段

Just gd company and supportive. I feel like everyone is just so diff, there r always gonna be things u like or don't like. So at the end of the day, it's Abt whether we can accept the things that we don't like. Or just being able to accept and respect the diff

body:
给人温暖

让肢体语言先于理性开口
    - 严肃和僵硬往往源于身体处于防御状态
    - 微微放松肩膀、将紧咬的下颌松开、让眼神带上一丝笑意。
     身体的松弛会直接传递给对方一种安全感，比任何理性的语言都管用

把“解决问题”切换成“接住情绪”
    - 温暖的替代方案： “听到你这么说，我能感觉到你当时挺委屈/挺不容易的……”

多用“自我暴露”来卸下防备
过于理性的人常常习惯藏起自己的脆弱和不确定。试着主动分享一些无伤大雅的小窘迫、小真实，或者你当时的真实感受。这种适度的“不完美”和坦诚，是拉近心理距离、产生人情味的催化剂。

---
Title: #self
---

最重要的是自我认知

魅力就是
  - 自信姿态展现自己本来的面目
  - 很相信自己有魅力

把自己最舒服的状态活出来

自信稳定确定的做自己
   - 足够的了解自己
      看见自己的特质
      找到让他发光的环境
      用自信把他交出去

并不是所有的事都是你的问题

Title: #info
---

当对方讲自己的story, view的时候，
    - 在香港， 表达往往偏高效， 直接且带有试探性

先通过肯定对方的情绪或存在来建立安全感（接住），
然后再用你的好奇心或思考去开拓话题的边界（延展）
    -  先停顿，比如点头，眼神， 传递： 我听到了
    -   接住 情绪或逻辑 - 承认对方有这样想的权力
        +  轻量认可： “这个视角挺特别的 …”
        +  复述确认： “听得出来，你对这件事挺有感触的 …”
        +  情绪共振： “确实，现在大家对这个都挺头疼的…”

    -  延展： 拋出好奇心 
        +  利用港人喜歡表達見解的特點，把話題往縱深處或輕鬆放下引
        +  追問契機： “是什麼讓你開始注意到這一點的？”
        +  類比延展： “這讓我想起我之前遇到過的一個情況，不知道你有沒有類似的感覺？”
        + 適度幽默/鬆弛： “你這麼一說，我得回去好好反思下我的消費觀”

    - 回歸鬆弛，享受碰撞
        + 当对方看到你稳稳接住了她的话，并且有兴趣进一步探讨时，她的防御心也会自然卸下

善用“缓冲”
    -  “这个角度挺有意思，我之前还真没从这方面想过 …“
    -  “你这么说倒提醒我，让我想一想 …”

把对方观点“抛回”给她
    -  如果不确定对方是否在试探，最好 反问或复述来拓展话题
    -  “听起来你对这件事很有主见， 是谁什么契机让你有这种看法”？
    -  “你的意思是  .., 对吗？“

建立“保留意见”的表达习惯
    - 如果当时没想好立场， 表达“需要沉淀”
    -  “我目前对这个还没完全定论， 不过你的观点对我很有启发”
    -  “这事信息量有些大，改天再给你聊”

    -  邀請一起想，一起分責

在壓力下保持冷靜和自在

看待壓力的方式

    - 害怕失去， 還是看到收穫 
        +  what’s there to lose?  every second you’re there you’re gaining something 

    -  從不同角度看 “壓力” 跟 “掙扎” 
       + I love struggle actually, it makes me feel alive

       +  我喜歡全力以赴， 那個過程裡被逼出的自己
             -  這件事對你很重要，很有挑戰性， 你會怕自己搞砸；
                可是它真正留下來給你的東西其實跟你最後有沒有成功沒有什麼關係

                 你會在那裡面能看到自己能承受多少，能長出能找出什麼東西來；

                  成不成功只是其中你能拿到的一個結果而已，而且那個結果前後都不完全在你的掌控之下；

                  那個結果哪一天就不見了，可是你在那個過程中的成長沒有任何人任何情況可以拿得走；
                  它是你的就是你的

             - 這件事對你越重要，越困難，你的壓力就會越大，
               壓力越大，只要你願意全心投入，它能從你身上逼出來的勇氣跟韌性就會越多，不管最後結果如何，
               這就是為什麼會說 她在那裡的每一秒都在得到

       +  表演的當下 她必須拿出百分之百， 拿出最好的自己， 付出自己的最多；
           她說除了滑冰， 生活裡幾乎沒有任何其他的時刻需要她付出百分之百；
           少了那份百分之百，生活其實蠻平淡的；
           滑冰那個巨大的挑戰是唯一讓她能遇到最強大的自己的地方

     - 分辨  在乎 VS 執著
        + I connect with everything, but I’m not attached to anything

        +  連結: 我想把這個體驗送給你們 
              - 付出
              - 把心力留在真正使得上力的地方，那就是他的付出，他的努力，他表演當下的狀態
                而且會影響他想要藉由滑冰送出去的那個體驗；
              而那些他無法掌控的像輸贏或是裁判的分數，他就不在上面多浪費心力，

             -  執著：  一定需要你們被打動，不然我就白來了

善意 VS 操縱 
    - 出發點
         +   為你好： 對方關注你的成長和自主權， 允許你犯錯
         +   操縱：  對方關注的是 如何讓你順從他們的意願

    -  邊界
          +   為你好：  使用客觀建議， 尊重你的個人邊界
          +    操縱

    -  情緒體驗
          +    為你好：  對話後你感到被支持，被理解
          +    操縱：  對話後你感到焦慮，困惑

互利 VS 剝削
    - 手段透明度
       +   為你好：  對方的意圖和訴求是 明牌 。
              他會坦誠說： “這樣做對我也有好處，但我認為對你同樣有價值，我們可以一起做”
       +   操縱：  對方可以隱瞞自己的目的，甚至用“全是為了你”做偽裝

   -  權力與選擇的對等
       +    為你好：  你有權利隨時喊停； 對方即便因為你拒絕而感到失落，也會尊重你的獨立決策
       +    操縱：  如果你試圖推出或提出修改，對方會通過情緒懲罰，利益綑綁或道德綁架，讓你覺得你”背叛“他

   -  陰性成本的承擔者
       +    為你好： 双方共同承担风险与付出，或者付出的比例是匹配、自愿的
       +     操縱： 所有的隐性成本、情绪消耗或潜在风险全由你来承担，而对方几乎零风险、零代价地享受了最大的果实

              你無法忍受職場上那種 上一秒持保留意見，下一秒立刻逢迎上司的變臉，
              因為那對你來說是 “自我欺騙” 與 “不真實”

    -  自主性 與 邊界感
         +  渴望兩個獨立個體之間的對等交流  

         +  在心理上，你是一個獨立的決策者，而不是依附於他人情緒或集體風向的草
              -  這也是為什麼當別人迎合你，沒有自己主見時，會本能推開對方；
                  過度迎合會剝奪你的自主空間，讓你被迫去承擔一段不對等，甚至需要你照顧對方情緒的關係

    -  accountability 
         + 希望別人對自己的話，自己的決定負責任

         +  在你的價值觀裡，當你做出一項決定（例如答應出席聚會）或給出一個承諾時，你對它是有心理帳本的
              - 覺得既然做了決定，後續的變動需要有足夠合理、透明的交代。你對自己和他人都有著這種「對行為結果負責」的期待。

    -  允許別人有 “不完美‘的生存方式
          +  內在： 你對”真誠度“ 要求很高，容不下虛偽
          +   外圓的外在表現：  理解職場或集體中有的人為了生存，有的人習慣隨波逐流；
                你不需要去矯正他們， 也不必在內心給予過重的審判。
                看清他們的模式，然後在心理輕輕隔開距離，把能量留給那些同樣真誠，值得深交的人

    - 在群體互動中， 學會 “先接納情緒，再表達立場”
         +  內在： 你對那種見風使舵，盲目附和的人感到反感或不屑
         +  外圓： 面對讓你看不慣的人或行為，你不需要當場翻白眼或冷臉。

         +  如果是純粹的人情往來（例如幫忙、送禮），就用情感的邏輯去對待

         +  及時止損，把你的能量留給那些即使在利益面前也能保持體面與尊重的人

學習二點：
1/對AGI預期
2/開基金同公司相同，寫一個清楚嘅計劃方案

Hi Amos，10/4 號 行山你去嗎？

對了，也一直在研究市場， 對於AGI前景的快速進展,  正逐漸從軟體轉向 硬體， 安全，能源 ...。 
之前看你分享的基金影片好感觸，我也在研究這塊的機會，不知道你有沒有留意這方面的機會？

我自己在整理一些筆記，不知道你有沒有興趣？

我這陣子自己琢磨了一下：既然 AGI 的發展已經逼近實體極限，我就在想，試下用常規公司主體，把方向轉向 AI 基礎設施、能源這類實體供應鏈去做股票配置。
自己整理了一套邏輯，不知道你對這塊有沒有興趣？得閒 WhatsApp 交流下，順便聽聽你有什麼需要注意的盲點和風控。

我可以寫份 計劃方案給你看看可以嗎？

---
Title: #self
---

明算帐  VS  踩过界
    - 在大额财务或合伙， 要明算账

    - 在日常生活 上， 保持 随性， 不过度计较

---
Title: #self
---

为什么真正决定情绪的，往往不是事情本身
我们如何为一件中性的事情配上痛苦的“注释和旁白”

情绪为什么会让思考变味

如何用一口呼吸，为自己创造选择的空间

一层层追问， 自己到底在害怕什么
 恐惧

---
Title: #self
---

当责与靠谱 对冲 物质 不对等
    - 答应的事情就一定做到，做事有交代，遇事不推卸责任

建立平等的心理边界， 拒绝 卑微
     -  我有我的专业尊严，我的生活原则

把 经济差距转化为 “可见的 成长斜率”

精准借力， 寻找现实中的商业与成长导师
     - 在香港，建立优质的人脉和商业视野很重要

     -  如何在这个城市 实现 阶级跃升与 事业突破

     -  学会用 专业， 真诚和靠谱去赢得周围前辈的欣赏

---
Title: #self
---

Coaching 

会听
    - 前提是 敞开的
    - 话来之后， 落下， 也不要马上去评判
    - 止住噪音， being there 
   - 

听清问题： 做别人的镜子，而不是做海绵
    - 不要听到问题就回答
       +  吸收，不要马上去评判， 或者 想对策或行动
       +  然后问问题
       +  然后去确认， 就是你来问他，你听到的那个真的问题是这个吗？ 还有别的吗？
           - 这样会让别人去思考

    - 带着善意，放下评判；
    用各种可能性去看眼前这个人，哪怕对方认为没有可能性；
    她可能需要有人告诉她，她还有别的可能性，你不一定要陷在这一个地方

    - 不要着急给你认为很简单的答案
     相信每个人如果他愿意看的话，他都可以有能力找到自己的答案的；
     我们要做的事情 其实是帮他找到他那个答案，作为他对话的伙伴

    - 别人说的话，很多时候是她自己内心的投射

听见情绪： 意见事情背后的情绪，以及情绪后面的需求
    -  听别人这个情绪后面有什么需求没有被满足，没有被看见，没有被尊重
        或者 说被trigger了什么，哪些东西是他特别不敢碰的

Root ： 心法
    -  眼前的人眼前的事就是我的道场

    -  一个人跟我对话的时候，这就是我的道场

    -  这是唯一的真实
        +   只有当下的这个人，面前的这件事情 实际上是各种机缘会合，发生在你眼前面的，这是唯一的真实

        +    缘起： 此刻在我面前的这个人， 他不是偶然出现的， 
         他是带着他的家庭经历，他一代一代前面的故事，他的恐惧，他的伤口，他的喜悦走到这里的，而我也是一样的；
         我们彼此在这个时候相遇，他是无数姻缘聚在一起的一次短暂交汇
        +  此刻的这个人这件事就是 宇宙推到我面前的，让我来进入当下的地方，修炼自己的地方

    - 见众生见自己
        + 见自己就是 知道我看见的别人 其实是经过了自己的滤镜的
        +  见众生 就是 知道每个人都有他的来路

我现在用什么样的状态跟她待一会

把每一次约会
当成在收集有趣人生故事
    - 摆脱 “非要有完美结局‘的执念， 就算被拒绝也不受伤

body:
notes on research
    research
    - 训练和考察他们检索寻求信息的能力、基于充分的信息进行推理判断的能力
    - 试图寻找史料，尽可能阅读多方观点，搭建自己的推理论证框架来得出独立结论

notes on problem-solving skills
   建立自己做事的方法论
    - TODO
    - 以目前的知识能力, 建立一个方法系统, 试图解决一类问题
    - 然后, 通过一个个问题的套用, 会发现系统中许多不足之处, 刺激方法系统的演进
    - 当方法系统演进不了的时候, 就去大量阅读, 借用别人的方法来刺激

   解决“复杂，未知问题”的能力
    - 自己做的具体事务背后，终极目标是什么，或者这件事情对组织的价值究竟是什么
    - 是否在现有位置上，看到更长远的事情 - 是否愿意跳出现有框架，去做创新思考，解决更复杂的问题，以及去领悟问题背后的意义
    - 决定差异的，是你的高度，和面临那些未知的挑战与问题


   解决问题的能力
    - 从现状出发，确定解决的目标是什么，再设定一个有解决价值的课题，然后付诸实际


   构想力 - 限定问题的能力
    - 一般问题 转化为  非常有用的子问题
    - 准确地限定问题关键点， 确定问题的焦点 <- 研究的构想力
    - 对问题限定并给出定义的练习 -> 决定问题的构思范围
    - 能否将想到的问题简单到最合适的程度，省略到什么程度是关键

   最初的想法的基础上， 添加附加东西，使之升华的水平才是决定胜负的关键

   真正的能力是解决现实生活中具体问题的能力
    - 从实际问题出发，自己思考，调研，解决，得出结果
    - 培养学生独立思考问题， 下功夫求解，寻找答案的能力
    - 思考现实生活中的问题，然后产生各种各样的疑问，进而再去解决
    - “如果... ,你会怎么做？”


notes on critical thinking
    "批判性" 是指思辨式的评判，多是建设性的
    理性分析，精确求证
    批判性思维除了要求在逻辑上、统计上不犯错误之外，更重要的是要想别人没有想过的问题，问别人没有问过的问题  ，并且要刨根问底，探究深层次、根本性的原因
   

notes on ideas

    相关性不等于因果性
     + 但是现在的大部分研究都是在论证相关性的，通过研究相关性来寻找其背后的机制，这是是推导出因果的基础,要直接论证因果性难度实在是太高，而且确定性的推论本来也不符合科学的要求。所以大家以后不要看到一篇研究相关性的论文就说它不科学

notes on taste
    如何提升研究品味，判断哪些工作是重要的，哪些不重要，可能是困扰我们这些年轻研究人员的一个重要问题。我在清华读硕士的时候，导师应明生教授推荐过一个方法，读科学史 -- 看ACM网站上对图灵奖工作的介绍，看google scholar里引用次数很多的文章有什么样的特点 -- 受益很多。

notes on research - creative, thoughtful original engineering research
    How to come up with research ideas:
    - 1) Find an existing research area you're interested in
    - 2) Find a paper in the area, check out the research they cite/cite them
    - 3) Keep reading until you have a Q: "What would happen if I tried X?"
    - 4) Try X  


    idea
     + mini-proposal
       - 3 project suggestions
       - 1 sentence

     + proposal
       - one page
       - what's your idea, and how do u plan to pursue it?

     + partial draft
       - 3 pages: Introduction, background, baseline results and a literature review

     + presentation
       - 5 minutes

     + final paper
       - 4 pages

    execution

    writing

    Example
     - The initial one-page proposal, which should describe the problem that you plan to solve, what resources (code, data, etc.) are available to help you solve it, and a very rough plan of work. We will try to offer constructive feedback at this point.

     - The partial draft in a single four-page document (not counting references and contribution statement). This should essentially be a near-final draft of your paper (in NAACL 2018 style) with the results, analysis, and conclusion sections missing. It should contain a link to your public GitHub repo, which should show evidence that you have implemented everything you’ll need to be able to run your experiments.

     - The presentation. You will be asked to give a very short presentation (likely 3–5 minutes) on the last day of class explaining the key result of your paper.

social skills
    独立研究员
     - 独立 不等于 一个人
     - 独立意味着你有所有权，需要自己收集知识，形成想法，然后拿这些东西和所有能提供帮助的人对话
     - Independent does not mean alone. Independent means figuring out the right questions to ask, finding the right people to ask, and taking the initiative to make it happen

    direction
    一个年轻的研究生最重要的一件事情是什么？
     - 其实不是你学到哪些技术，而是要使你自己走进未来五年、十年有大发展机会的领域，这才是你做研究生时所要达到的目标。”

确定的方向
    重要的问题和挑战
    即将成为热门 - 影响重大
    高风险

Proposal <-  确定的问题 <-  确定的方向

   source <- web of science and google scholar
    - Conferences and journal
    - keywords -> 浏览摘要 来 筛选

   review paper - 文献综述

教訓
   總是想着把基礎打紮實，從而在理解和復現已有的技術上花了太多的時間

body:
ideas 
  podcast + iot device  


about beauty  
what's beauty?  why do people enjoy the beauty?  

why do math models fit in with the natural world  
many real world phenomena can be modeled with analytic distributions, why?  

Analytic distributions are abstractions, which means they leave out details that are considered irrelevant.  

Analytic models are also a form of data compression. When a model fits a dataset well, a small set of parameters can summarize a large amount of data.   

Models are useful if they capture the relevant aspects of the real world and leave out unneeded dtails. But what is "relevant" or "unneeded" depends on what you are planning to use the model for. 



reference

title: [Updating] The Pragmatic Programming
excerpt: ch7 Before the project digging for requirements - make the requirement the general statement , and give the developers the policy information as an example - discover the underlying reason why users…
excerpt_search: ch7 Before the project digging for requirements - make the requirement the general statement , and give the developers the policy information as an example - discover the underlying reason why users…
body:
ch7 Before the project 
 digging for requirements 
    - make the requirement the general statement , and give the developers the policy information as an example 

    - discover the underlying reason why users do a particular, rather than just the way 
      + documenting the reasons behind requirements 
      + your dev has to solve the business problem, not just meet the stated requirements 

    - propose the concept of use cases as a basis for discussions - the developers, the end users, and project sponsors 

    - requirements are need 
      + accurately reflects the business need 

      + capture the underlying semantic invariants as requirements, and document the specific as policy 

      + abastractions live longer than details 

The Pragmatic Approach 
 The evails of duplication adn othrogonality


The basic tools  - tools amplify your talent
 Invest in your own basic toolbox
    
 Plain Text is that standard
    Our base material is knowledge. We express that knowledge in our designs, implementations, test, and documents. The best format for storing knowledge persistently is plain text.
    
 Power editing 
    Using one Editor could manipulate text as effortlessly as possible. we should know it very well, and use it for all editing tasks.  
      
 Debugging - fix the problem, not the blame
     - debugging is just problem solving, and attack it as such
     - visualize the data -> get a good look at the data it is operating on
     - Tracing -> the state of a program or a data structure over time 
     - Don't assume it, prove it; and how to improve it 
     - master one text manipulation language 


TODO 

reference
 The Pragmatic Programmer by Andrew Hunt & David Thomas

body:
Raymond ZHAO Wenlong is a product-minded engineer, and director@Bean based in Hong Kong now.  

Outside of reading and tech, he also likes  Philosophy, Nature,  dog/horse/bird, Film,  and  Color.  

Some of his favorite quotes:

- "Life is too short to worry about stupid things. Fall in love.  Study, think, create and grow."  - Richard Feynman  
- "What makes you vulnerable makes you strong and beautiful"
- "The good life is one inspired by love and guided by knowledge" - Bertrand Russell

He was a Technical Officer at HSU, RA in (CUHK, CityU, and HKBU), Tech Lead at HKCREO (a Fintech startup), and Lead Software Engineer at Alcatel-Lucent (now Nokia).

Raymond got his M.S. in Computer Science at Chinese University of Hong Kong and BEng in Electronic and Information Engineering at WuHan University.

title: About Coaching
excerpt: Note - 了解人性 life coash Coaching as a leader - You don't need to have all the solutions - You do need to be able to connect with people, to inspire them to do their best, and to help them search insid…
excerpt_search:
Note - 了解人性 life coash Coaching as a leader - You don't need to have all the solutions - You do need to be able to connect with people, to inspire them to do their best, and to help them search insid…
Note - 瞭解人性 life coash Coaching as a leader - You don't need to have all the solutions - You do need to be able to connect with people, to inspire them to do their best, and to help them search insid…
body:
Note

- 了解人性

life coash

Coaching as a leader

- You don't need to have all the solutions
    - You do need to be able to connect with people, to inspire them to do their best,
      and to help them search inside and discover their own answers

- It's unrealistic and ill-advised to expect leaders to have all the answers
    - By using coaching, leaders can still be effective without knowing all the answewrs
      and without telling employees what to do
    - Coaching is about connecting with people, inspiring them to do their best, and helping them to grow
        - Coaching is also about challenging people to come up with the answers they require on their own

- Asking open-ended questions
    - init "so, where would you like to start?"
        - may well set some limits to the conversation
        - "I'm not prepared to talk about the budget today"
        - "I'd like to discuss last week's meeting, in addition to what's on your list"

    - identify different modes of inquiry
        - diagnostic inquiry
            - focusing the other person's attention on specific aspects of their story,
              such as feelings and reactions, underlying causes or motives, or actions taken or contemplated
            - "You seem frustrated with Chris. How's that relationship going?"
            - "It sounds like there's been some tension on your team. What do you think is happening?"
            - "That's an ambitious goal for that project. How are you planning to get there?"
        - Confrontational inquiry
            - Challenge aspects of their story by introducting new ideas and hypotheses
            - "You've been talking about Chris's shortcomings. How might you be contributing to the problem?"
            - "That's an exciting plan, but it has a lot of moving parts. What happens if you're behind schedule?"

- Listen
    - make the other person truly feel heard
        - eye contact, facial expressions, gestures, tics

- Empathize
    - Empathy is the ability not only to comprehend another person's point of view,
      but also to vicariously experience their emotions

    - Feeling and expressing empathy is critical to helping the other person defuse their embarrassment
        - shame - the intensely painful feeling or experience of believing that we are flawed and therefore unworthy of love and belonging
        - when employees need your help they are likely experiencing some form of shame

    - traps when trying to express empathy
        - compare our issues to theirs (my problem's worse)
        - try to be overly positive (look on the bright side)
        - leap to problem-solving while ignoring what they're feeling in the moment

    - expressing empathy need not prevent you from holding people to high standards
        - After you've acknowledged an employee's struggles and feelings,
          they're more likely to respond to your efforts to motivate improved performace

- reference
    - How Great Coaches Ask, Listen, and Empathize

Shame & Empathy

- connection
    - forge meaningful authentic relationships with other people
    - connection is what breathes lives and gives meaning to our lives

- Vulnerability
    - Open, willing to share not only our strengths with people, but our struggles that moves us towards empathy

- Empathy
    - Empathy is about being vulnerable with people in their vulnerability

- Shame
    - Shame is the feeling that we are fundamentally flawed or unworthy
        - Shame is a belief that we are the problem
            - Shame breeds fear, blame, and disconnection

        - Fear arises as a protective resposne to that shame
            - We fear being seen, judged, or cast out because shame tells us we're not good enough

        - Fear of vulnerability
            - Shame makes openness feel dangerous.
              Vulnerability could lead to more shame, so we fear being emotionally honest.

            - Build empathy
                - Set boundaries
                    - openness doesn't mean oversharing.
                      You can be authentic while protecting your emotional space
                - Sharing with trusted people can dissolve shame
                - Remind yourself that imperfection is human

        - Fear of judgment
            - Shame convinces us we'll be criticized or humiliated, so we fear situations where we might be evaluated

        - Fear of failure
            - Shame links failure to personal inadequacy, making us afraid to try, risk, or grow

    - The awareness of human separation, without reunion by love - is the source of shame
        - It is at the same time the source of guilt and anxiety

    - How do I tell these stories which is the only way
      that we get out from underneath shame?
        - I can't let you see these pieces of me
          because I fear that it will cause disconnection

    - courage, compassion & connection
        - courage meant to speak your mind with your heart to tell your story
        - how do I stay open and sit in that with you as opposed to moving into blame if you share your story with me?

reference

        - Coaching is also about challenging people to come up with the answers they require on their own

            - Challenge aspects of their story by introducting new ideas and hypotheses
            - "You've been talking about Chris's shortcomings. How might you be contributing to the problem?"

excerpt_search: > An introduction of Hash function Introduction - a set of N items - we can sort them with binary search in O(log N) time using a structure(i.e, an array) of O(N) space . - while a hashing technique…
body:
> An introduction of Hash function

Introduction

-   a set of N items

    -   we can sort them with binary search in O(log N) time using a structure(i.e, an array) of O(N) space .

    -   while a hashing technique can consume O(N) space, and answers
        a dictionary query in O(1) expected time.

-   We can reference key-value pairs using arrays by doing arithmetic operations to transform keys into array indices. Thus there are two steps

    -   compute a hash function that transfers the search key into an array index

    -   collision-resolution process that deals with two or more different keys (may hash to the same array index)

hash functions

-   hashing

    -   the hash function h maps the university U of keys into the $T[0...m-1]$

        -   $h : U -> T = {0, 1, ..., m-1}$

    -   uniform hashing assumption: assume that any given element in U is equally likely to hash into
        any of the m slots, independently of where any other element has hashed to .
        -   For any diff integers $k1$ and $k2$, $Pr(h(k1)=h(k2)) \leq 1/m$

-   a good hash function

    -   deterministic: equal keys produce the same hash value
    -   efficient to compute
    -   uniformly distribute the keys among the integer values [0, m-1]
        -   each key is equally likely to be hashed to one of m indices
        -   The reason for this requirement is that the cost of hashing-based methods goes up sharply
            as the number of collisions-pairs of inputs that are mapped to the same hash value- increases.
            If some hash values are more likely to occur than others, a larger fraction of the lookup
            operations will have to search through a larger set of colliding table entries. [2]
        -   [Note]: the random is uniform

-   hashing by division h(k) = k mod m

    -   map a key k into one of m slots

    -   if we know that the keys are random real numbers k
        independently and uniformly distributed in the range $0 \leq k < 1$
        then, the hash function: $h(k) = floor(km)$

    -   the division method can give good results, assumimg that a prime
        number k that is unrelated to any patterns in the distribution of keys .

-   hashing by multiplication

-   universal hashing
    -   TODO

for the collision-resolution process

-   collision: two keys may hash to the same slot

-   hashing with separate chaining (link structure)

    -   linked list of the key-value pairs whose keys hash to that index

    -   the basic idea is to choose m to be sufficiently large that the lists are sufficiently short to enable
        efficient search through a two-step process

-   hashing with linear probing

    -   open-addressing: store N key-value pairs in a hash table of size m>N

    -   the idea is that rather than using memory space for references in linked lists, we use it for
        the empty entries in the hash table, which mark the ends of probe sequences

hashtables vs other dictionary implementations

-   choosing a good capacity m

    -   We can choose the table size m to be sufficiently small that we do not waste a huge area of
        contiguous memory with empty chains but sufficiently large that we donot waste time searching through
        long chains.

-   hashtables are sometimes good because

    -   the keys do not have to come from an ordered type
    -   in practice we can set things up for constant-time performance

-   hashtables aren't always the best choice because
    -   you cannot easily read things out in a sorted order, assuming these was such an order
    -   you can't really get a good hash function that be can computed quickly, so they're usally
        bad for small dictionaries
    -   resizing is very expensive, and probably can't be used in most real-time systems

reference

-   Juraj Hromkovic - ch3 "Design and Analysis of Randomized Algorithms"
-   Robert Sedgewick and Kevin Wayne - ch3.4, "Algorithms"
-   hashtable
-   hash function

title: About Priority Queue
excerpt: Stack: FILO (first in, last out) [1] - Stored in computer RAM - stack grows and shrinks as functions push and pop local variables; Variables are allocated and freed automatically . - CPU manage the m…
excerpt_search: Stack: FILO (first in, last out) [1] - Stored in computer RAM - stack grows and shrinks as functions push and pop local variables; Variables are allocated and freed automatically . - CPU manage the m…
body:
Stack: FILO (first in, last out) [1]

-   Stored in computer RAM
-   stack grows and shrinks as functions push and pop local variables;
    Variables are allocated and freed automatically .
-   CPU manage the memory, reading from and writing to stack variables is very fast

Heap [1]

-   Stored in computer RAM
-   heap variables are essentially global in scope.
-   Heap memory is slightly slower to be read from and written to,
    because one has to use pointers to access memory on the heap.
-   If we need variables like arrays and structs that can change size dynamically,
    then we will likely need to allocate them on the heap.

queue : FIFO

stack : FILO (first in, last out)

Priority Queue

-   The case
    -   We collect a set of items, then process the one with the largest key, then perhaps collect more items,
        then process the one with the current largest key.

    -   a collection in which items can be added at any time, but the only item that can be removed is the one
        with the highest priority.
-   The implementations

    -   unordered array/linked-list:

        -   To insert: push in the stack. O(1)
        -   To remove the max: exchange the MAX with the item at the end, and then delete that one. o(n)

    -   ordered array/linked-list:

        -   for insert to move larger entries on the right position,thus keeping the keys in the order array. o(n)
        -   The MAX is always at the end. O(1)

    -   binary heap [2]

        -   a binary tree is heap-ordered if the key in each node >= the keys in the node's two children [3].
        -   To insert: exchanging the node with its parent to restore the heap condition
        -   To remove:

            -   take the key off the top;
            -   put the item at the end of the heap to the top,
            -   and then sink through the heap with the key to restore the heap condition

        -   In a heap, the highest (or lowest) priority item is always stored at the root, hence the name "heap".
            A heap is not a sorted structure and can be regarded as partially ordered . There is no particular
            relationship among ndoes on any given level, even among the siblings [4].

        -   A heap is useful data structure when we need to remove the object with the highest (or lowest) priority.

        -   O(logN)

[1]: http://gribblelab.org/CBootcamp/7MemoryStackvsHeap.html "stack and heap"
[2]: http://cs.lmu.edu/~ray/notes/pqueues/ "priority queue"
[3]: http://algs4.cs.princeton.edu/24pq/ "Priority Queues"
[4]: http://www.cs.cmu.edu/~adamchik/15-121/lectures/Binary%20Heaps/heaps.html "priority queues"

body:
notes   
 bible reading 
    - 和耶稣基督的关系  
        + 只需要 依照福音书的教诲，以耶稣为榜样，在尘世中生活，工作，这就是善行；  
        无必要为求择而格外行善事  

    - 把神学和哲学结合起来 
        + 把基督的思想当成引导人过有道德的尘世生活的智慧    
        + 人生在世， 要有意义地活着； 灵感启示和问题解释    
        + 相信人的精神生活的价值， 使人成为世界的中心  

    - 人文主义宗教 - 有理性的信仰  - 宽容  
        + 古典哲学追寻的善， 与基督思想的神圣性结合起来  
        + 耶稣基督的学说不需要批评， 它是神圣的，福音的哲学  
        + 从耶稣基督的行为中体会它的神圣性； 常人效法基督也可获得神圣性  

    - 约翰·加尔文的新教倫理  
        + 在尘世中尽自己的天职， 自强，自助，勤勉，守信，虔诚  
            -  人对天职（calling）负有责任       
            -  日常的经商活动，变成了响应上帝的召唤，为上帝的荣耀在尘世中尽职  
            -  勤奋的创造财富，是遵从上帝的最好方法  
            -  无论创造的财富是多少，都是对上帝的奉献，都是依从了上帝的旨意  
            -  个人创造的私有财产，以及对私有财产的保护 => 自由政府    
            -   “你看办事勤恳的人，必站在君王面前”   

        + 现世一切活动，是为了增加上帝的荣耀，不是为了赚取上帝的选择  
            - 上帝要求基督徒取得社会成就， 上帝的意旨，是要根据他的圣诫来组织社会生活， 
            因而尘世中基督徒的社会活动，完全是为了增加上帝的荣耀；  
            为社会的尘世生活而服务的职业劳作，就含有这一特性      

        + 上帝应许的唯一生存方式，是要完成个人在现世里所处地位赋予他的责任和义务    
            - 个人道德活动所能采取的最高形式，应是对其履行世俗事务的义务进行评价，
            不是要人们以苦修的禁娱主义超越世俗道德  
            - 人對天職負有責任    

        + 上帝幫助那些 自助的人     
            - 对得救坚定不疑的信念    
                + 既然不知道上帝的择选，就没必要去担心自己是否获得上帝的择选，也无必要为求择选而格外行善事   
                + 只需要依照福音書的教诲， 以耶稣基督为榜样，在尘世中生活，工作，这就是善行  


Learning  
 以神的眼光来看待自己的苦难    
    - “不要因为把我卖到这里自忧自恨，这是神差我在你们以先来，为要保全生命”  
    - 约瑟试探哥哥的内心，引領他們悔改，进而宽恕  
    
 约瑟 尽心去做事, 没有灰心    
    - ”耶和华与他同在，他就百事顺利“ 創世纪 39-2  
        + “the LORD was with Joseph and gave him success in everything he did“    
        + “耶和华使他手里所办的事都顺利”  創世纪 39-3  

    - 开始关心身边的人 - 服事王的酒政和膳长    
        + “但你得好处的时候，求你记念我，施恩与我，在法老面前提说我，救我处这监牢” 40-14  

    - the testing of your faith produces perseverance  
        + “因為知道你們的信心經過试验，就生忍耐； 但忍耐也当成功，使你们成全，完备，毫无缺欠” 雅各书1-3,4  
        + “because you know that the testing of your faith produces perseverance. Let perseverance finish its work so that you may be mature and complete, not lacking anything”
     
 做事尽力  
    - 雅各 做什么事情都很尽力    
        + 前半生 与人竞争  
    - “只剩下雅各一人” - 不安/恐惧  - 創世紀 32-24 

 爱上帝，服务他人  
    - kindness & love    
    - 上帝use me, 作为改变的一部分？  
        + 社会需要哪方面的改变？  

    - 神 放在雅各身上的各种磨练，是对他的盼望，以让他本性可以改变    
        + 比如 雅各的欺骗，自尊  

 以耶和华 引领我  
    - “我也与你同在。 你无论往哪里去，我必保佑你，领你归回这地，总不离弃你，直到我成全了向你所应许的。”  创世纪 28-15  

 上帝会供应你所需的信心

body:
[AI Synthesis]: Charm from the outside in: people judge behavior. Act as if you already are charming (or already feel the emotion you want); outward action triggers matching inner feeling.

Outside in vs inside out
 What matters is what people think you are.
 “Inside out” (American) vs “outside in” (European): change external behavior with skills that control the image others see.
 Behave as though you are happy or excited and others (and often you) will feel it.
 Worry less about the why; concentrate on the how — often easier and faster to change.
 Concentrate on how you can behave differently, not why you do things.

Behavior is everything
 You are ultimately judged by your behavior.
 People react to how they perceive you to behave, whatever your inner agenda.
 Concentrate on behaving exactly as if you were already a charming person.

Actions trigger feelings
 Pretend as if you already feel it until it becomes reality.
 Outward behavior creates the corresponding inner feeling; controlling actions helps create the emotions you want.
 Example: dress and act “well” and midmorning you feel better — behaviors of being well.

Actions
 Build skills that change external behavior and the personal image others see.
 Create a mental image of yourself as charming inside — then act accordingly outside.
 Act as if you already felt a particular way; actions soon trigger matching feelings.

 Act as if you already felt a particular way; actions soon trigger matching feelings.

excerpt: tips stress - focus on stress and 'feeling' - stress relates to rhythm and intonation - think about not just individual sounds but also think about the overall feeling of the sentence. study mouths m…
excerpt_search: tips stress - focus on stress and 'feeling' - stress relates to rhythm and intonation - think about not just individual sounds but also think about the overall feeling of the sentence. study mouths m…
body:
tips  
 stress 
    - focus on stress and 'feeling'   
    - stress relates to rhythm and intonation    
    - think about not just individual sounds but also
  think about the overall feeling of the sentence.   

 study mouths movement  
 repetition   

pitch 
 raised the pitch for the stress words, and dropped it at the end, and played with the level so every syllable was a little higher or a little lower than previous word . 

 Intonation - emojis 
    - understand the hidding meaning 
   
    - GPS or mapping 
    - "that was good" - rise, fall, and rise 
    - "that was good" - rise, falling at the end <- negative 
  

Stress - longer, louder, and higher 
 verb, adj, and noun 
 de-stress: relaxed and short -> function word

Intonation, Linking, Rhythm
 The shape of stress  

 the schwa sound  
    - vowel -> /ə/  
   
 stress-timed language  
    - to -> /tə/ or /də/ 
    - because of ->  /kəz ə/
    - for -> /fər/
    - and -> /ən/
    - them -> /əm/
    - at -> /ət|/
    - can -> /kən/
    - are -> /ər/
    - was -> /wəz/
    - that -> /ðət|/
    - your -> /yər/
    - at the -> /ət| ðə/
    - her -> /ər/
    - it's okay -> /tsou 'kei/
    - as -> /əz/ as tall as
    - was -> /wəz/ 
  
    - You're welcome /jər' wel kəm/ 
  
    - WHAT DID Reduction
        + what did -> /'wʌt| did/ or /wʌd/
        + what did he -> /'wʌd i/
        + what did you -> /wʌdʒ ə/
    - helping verb
        + do -> /də/
        + does -> /dəz/
    - should, would, could
        + should -> /∫əd/ or /∫ə/
        + would -> /wəd/
        + could -> /kəd/ or /kə/
    - shoulda,coulda,woulda 
        + should have -> /∫ud ə/
        + should not have -> /∫ud ən ə/
        + could have -> /kud ə/
        + would have -> /wu dəv/
    - can, cann't
        + can -> /kən/
        + cannot -> /kænt/
    - [are]()
        + are -> /ər/
        + were -> /wər/
    - what
        + /wʌt|/

    - the
        + at the -> /ət | ðə/
        + is the -> tongue pushes on back of the teeth
        + with the -> /wiθ ð|ə/

    - [?]()
        + what do you think ? -> /wʌ də jə/  

    - whaddya /wa:dəyə/
        + What do you ... ? -> 


Connected speech 
 [Change vibration] [7]
    - [t] + [y] -> [t∫]
        + I got you? -> /ai GAt∫yə/

 h-deletion
    - "he" -> /iy/
    - "him" -> /im/
    - "his" -> /iz/
    - "her" -> /ər/
    - "has" -> /æz/
    - "have" -> /æv/ /əv/
        + Did he get it? -> /Di-diy Ge-dit/
        + Did he get the new car? -> /DId hiy/ -> /DI-diy/


write what you hear  


improve listening  
  study reducation
  study linking
    - he always /hi(y) 'ɔl weiz/
   study native speech
  write what you hear
  try Youglish -> YouGlish

excerpt: > An overview of Natural Language Processing and Linguistics Human language A human language is a symbolic signaling system. Most words are just symbols for an extra-linguistic entity: the word is a…
excerpt_search: > An overview of Natural Language Processing and Linguistics Human language A human language is a symbolic signaling system. Most words are just symbols for an extra-linguistic entity: the word is a…
body:
> An overview of Natural Language Processing and Linguistics

Human language

A human language is a symbolic signaling system. Most words are just symbols for an extra-linguistic entity: the word is a signifier that maps to a signified (idea or thing).

The symbols of language can be encoded like voice, gesture, writing, etc via continuous signals to the brain. Thus exploring the continuous encoding signals can be psychology or cognitive problems (like "What is thought?", even the fundational challenge: Turing Test ).

<del>The core questions in human language are that problems, architectures, cognitive science, and the details of human language, how it is learned, processed, and how it changes .</del>

About Languages

-   phonetics
-   phonology - the study of the sound patterns of human languages

    -   word stress - vowels in unstressed syllables are pronounced as schwa /ə/
    -   To produce a stressed syllable, one may change the pitch, make the syllable louder, or make it longer
    -   Intonation may reflect syntactic or semantic differences

-   morphology - rules of word formation
    -   Morphemes - the mini units of meaning
-   syntax
-   semantics - the linguistic meaning

    -   lexical semantics

-   pragmatics - how context affects meanings

Word vectors

-   produce dense vector representations based on the context of words
-   Count-based like TF-IDF
-   Distributed Representations

Word embeddings

-   Word semantic meaning
    -   hypernyms (is-a) relationships and synonym sets (like wordnet)
    -   word vectors encode valuable semantic information. For example, Word2Vec Model knows a word from its neighbors, or vice versa, which relies on the linguistic hypothesis, distributional similarity (similar words have similar context).

Language Modeling - a probabilistic model of word sequences

-   N-gram
-   Finite automata and RNN
-   LSTM Networks

Parsing and tree structure

reference

-   自動機理論
-   Computational Linguistics I
-   Computational Linguistics - fall2016
-   https://github.com/oxford-cs-deepnlp-2017/lectures
-   CS224n: Natural Language Processing with Deep Learning
-   NLP best practices
-   A look at the importance of Natural Language Processing
-   Manning (2016). Computational Linguistics and Deep Learning. Computational Linguistics
-   Language Files: Materials for an Introduction to Language and Linguistics
-   Deep Natural Language Processing
-   A Primer on Neural Network Models for Natural Language Processing
-   Word2Vec Tutorial - The Skip-Gram Model

The symbols of language can be encoded like voice, gesture, writing, etc via continuous signals to the brain. Thus exploring the continuous encoding signals can be psychology or cognitive problems (like "What is thought?", even the fundational challenge: Turing Test ).

<del>The core questions in human language are that problems, architectures, cognitive science, and the details of human language, how it is learned, processed, and how it changes .</del>

About Languages

-   phonetics
-   phonology - the study of the sound patterns of human languages

    -   word stress - vowels in unstressed syllables are pronounced as schwa /ə/
    -   To produce a stressed syllable, one may change the pitch, make the syllable louder, or make it longer
    -   Intonation may reflect syntactic or semantic differences

-   morphology - rules of word formation
    -   Morphemes - the mini units of meaning
-   syntax
-   semantics - the linguistic meaning

    -   lexical semantics

-   pragmatics - how context affects meanings

Word vectors

-   produce dense vector representations based on the context of words
-   Count-based like TF-IDF
-   Distributed Representations

Word embeddings

-   Word semantic meaning
    -   hypernyms (is-a) relationships and synonym sets (like wordnet)
    -   word vectors encode valuable semantic information. For example, Word2Vec Model knows a word from its neighbors, or vice versa, which relies on the linguistic hypothesis, distributional similarity (similar words have similar context).

excerpt_search: [AI Synthesis]: Under limited control and high stakes, we believe stories we want to be true. Incomplete views become complete narratives—and that gap is dangerous. Wanting truth to be true Many thin…
body:
[AI Synthesis]: Under limited control and high stakes, we believe stories we want to be true. Incomplete views become complete narratives—and that gap is dangerous.

Wanting truth to be true
 Many things feel true because we desperately want them to be true.
 An appealing fiction appears when you are smart, want solutions, but face limited control and high stakes.
 People chase huge outcomes partly because the possibility exists.
 The biggest risk: wanting something to be true so badly that forecasts miss reality entirely.

Protect with error, flexibility, independence
 Room for error, flexibility, and financial independence are indispensable defenses.
 The bigger the gap between what you want to be true and what you need to be true for an acceptable outcome, the more you protect yourself from appealing financial fiction.

Incomplete views, complete stories
 Everyone has an incomplete view of the world but forms a complete narrative to fill the gaps.
 People tell coherent stories from little they know.
 Most do not realize they misunderstand because explanations fit their limited experience.
 We want the complicated world to make sense—so we tell stories to fill blind spots.

Stories vs statistics
 The confident person who “knows” from what he sees can be wholly wrong because he cannot know stories inside everyone else’s head.

Actions
 When stakes are high, widen room for error before trusting a story that feels satisfying.
 List what you do not know explicitly before acting on a narrative that “makes sense.”

body:
[AI Synthesis]: Charm signals are mostly nonverbal: eye contact, eye flicks, head tilts and nods, open whole-body orientation, vocal and verbal reassurances. Delivery outweighs words (body ~55%, tone ~38%, words ~7%).

Eye contact and the flick
 Make direct, focused eye contact — especially when listening.
 Eyes flick eye-to-eye (or eyes–lips triangle); more eye activity reads as more engaged.
 Observe people; practice shifting gaze between their eyes.
 Look-aside: briefly shift gaze to the side of the face / ear, then back to mouth and eyes — never more than two or three seconds.
 In one-on-one, look at the other person’s eyes no more than ~85% of the time; in groups, shift gaze gently person to person.

Head, body, voice
 Nod while listening; tilt head to listen, straighten to speak.
 Combine vocal reassurances with eye contact and nodding (“I see,” “Really?”, “I agree, absolutely”).
 Keep the whole body turned toward the person; arms unfolded; sit upright (back off the chair).
 Soften voice and lean forward when engaged.
 Deeper vocal sounds suggest size and strength; higher sounds convey smallness and weakness.
 A smile can be heard and felt in your voice on the phone.
 You are judged by how you position your body; stay in control of the signals you send.
 Focus on delivery techniques.

Actions
 Practice excellent, focused eye contact when listening; flick gaze eye to eye.
 Small head tilt when someone speaks; whole body oriented; arms open.
 Sit up straight; soften voice; lean in when answering.
 Gently lower your voice toward deeper, warmer tones — don’t force it; vary tone up and down.
 Slow down and use silence.
 Speak warmly and gently; speak clearly, simply, and directly.

body:
Wiki Audit & Socratic Mirror Report
Last Run: 2026-09-06 10:20:26

> Deterministic scan: structure, red links, emotional tags, duplicate themes, Level-2 guidance.

> For cross-page cognitive lint, run make lint (one global LLM pass via skills/lint.md).

---

⚖️ Cognitive Lint (Global)

Cross-page contradictions

- [Cognitive Shift] Vulnerability vs. Strategic Self-Interest Protection  
  脆弱性领导 advocates genuine uncertainty and coach-style inquiry as trust-builders. 先利益后逻辑 and 利益安全与真实领导 frame "protecting the other's self-interest narrative" as a precondition for vulnerability — effectively making vulnerability a strategic move after securing the other's ego. The bridge principle (利益安全与真实领导) acknowledges the manipulation risk but doesn't resolve the core tension: is vulnerability a tactic deployed after ego-safety, or a stance that precedes calculation? The wiki holds both without a meta-principle for when each mode applies.

- [Cognitive Shift] Connection-First vs. Incentive-First Relating  
  连结式关系 declares relationships are for "共同体验与连结，而非审计付出". 商业算盘与激励 insists "生意先看清激励结构与算盘，再谈信任与脆弱". The profile explicitly flags these as "两条话语同库并存，尚未合成一条可操作的桥接原则". No principle defines the boundary conditions (e.g., "intimate vs. transactional", "infinite vs. finite game") or a switching heuristic.

- [Cognitive Shift] Freedom Maximization vs. Upward Management  
  From 公民话语与职场策略.md: "一边写自由最大化与叙事框架，一边练向上管理与识做分寸". The citizen-discourse frame (autonomy, narrative sovereignty) and the workplace-strategy frame (political savvy, reading the room) are documented as coexisting tensions with no synthesis. This mirrors the vulnerability/strategy split above at a higher abstraction layer.

Stale or unreconciled principles

- Unoperationalized Hypothesis  
  The Digital Twin Profile states: "已认账假设：你的關係模式可以被定義為一種『基於高度自主性的價值共創模式』". This L1 hypothesis (high-autonomy value co-creation) has no corresponding L2 principle, no decision rules, and no link to 连结式关系 or 商业算盘与激励. It sits as a recognized-but-unintegrated insight.

- Abstraction Level Mismatch  
  知识系统与自我维基 is a tooling/pipeline principle (raw→compression→wiki). The other five are human-dynamics principles. They live in the same principlesindex but operate at different ontological layers. No principle governs how the pipeline should capture, distill, or evolve the human-dynamics principles themselves (meta-distillation).

- Near-Duplicate Cluster: Self-Interest Protection  
  先利益后逻辑 (conf 0.84) and 利益安全与真实领导 (conf 0.82) share the same core mechanism: "secure ego/self-interest first, then logic/vulnerability". The latter adds the vulnerability caveat. They function as v1 and v2 of the same idea without explicit versioning or deprecation.

Emotional / behavioral patterns

- [Socratic Observation] Control-through-Framework Anxiety  
  Multiple principles reveal a pattern of managing relational uncertainty via pre-structured frames:  
  - Pipeline frame for knowledge (知识系统与自我维基)  
  - Ego-safety frame before logic (先利益后逻辑)  
  - Incentive-map frame before trust (商业算盘与激励)  
  - "Bridge" frame sequencing safety then vulnerability (利益安全与真实领导)  
  The recurring need to sequence and pre-condition suggests a deep discomfort with unstructured relational emergence — even as 脆弱性领导 and 连结式关系 nominally value openness and non-auditing connection.

- [Socratic Observation] Manipulation Paranoia as Design Constraint  
  利益安全与真实领导 explicitly names manipulation ("沦为操纵") and "裸逻辑伤人" as failure modes. This fear shapes the architecture: vulnerability is only permitted after strategic ego-protection. The wiki treats authenticity as dangerous unless gated — a self-fulfilling prophecy that may attract exactly the transactional dynamics it tries to engineer around.

- [Socratic Observation] Historical Integration Debt  
  The red-link report shows 70+ missing topics, heavily concentrated in 2015–2017 diaries, learning notes, and philosophy posts. The distillation pipeline (raw→compression→wiki) appears to have stalled on pre-2020 content. This creates a temporal blind spot: current principles are distilled mostly from recent inputs, while a decade of raw material remains unintegrated — potentially containing earlier versions of today's tensions.

Structural gaps & duplicate themes

| Gap / Duplicate | Evidence |
|----------------|----------|
| No domain-boundary principle | Personal (连结式关系) vs. business (商业算盘与激励) principles coexist without a "context-switching" or "domain-detection" rule. |
| No meta-principle for principle evolution | How does a principle get deprecated, versioned, or merged? 先利益后逻辑 → 利益安全与真实领导 happened organically but invisibly. |

  利益安全与真实领导 explicitly names manipulation ("沦为操纵") and "裸逻辑伤人" as failure modes. This fear shapes the architecture: vulnerability is only permitted after strategic ego-protection. The wiki treats authenticity as dangerous unless gated — a self-fulfilling prophecy that may attract exactly the transactional dynamics it tries to engineer around.

- [Socratic Observation] Historical Integration Debt  
  The red-link report shows 70+ missing topics, heavily concentrated in 2015–2017 diaries, learning notes, and philosophy posts. The distillation pipeline (raw→compression→wiki) appears to have stalled on pre-2020 content. This creates a temporal blind spot: current principles are distilled mostly from recent inputs, while a decade of raw material remains unintegrated — potentially containing earlier versions of today's tensions.

Structural gaps & duplicate themes

| Gap / Duplicate | Evidence |
|----------------|----------|
| No domain-boundary principle | Personal (连结式关系) vs. business (商业算盘与激励) principles coexist without a "context-switching" or "domain-detection" rule. |
| No meta-principle for principle evolution | How does a principle get deprecated, versioned, or merged? 先利益后逻辑 → 利益安全与真实领导 happened organically but invisibly. |
| Citizen/Workplace tension unprincipled | 公民话语与职场策略.md documents the split but produces no L2 operating rule. |
| Hypothesis orphan | "高度自主性的价值共创模式" has no L2 descendant, no test criteria, no link to existing principles. |
| Near-duplicate pair | 先利益后逻辑 + 利益安全与真实领导 = same core mechanism, different maturity. Consider merging with version note. |
| Pipeline blind spot | 知识系统与自我维基 governs tooling but not what gets distilled — no principle for "which raw posts deserve compression" or "how often to re-distill old clusters". |

Socratic Questions

1. When you "protect the other's self-interest narrative" before vulnerability, who is the actual beneficiary of that sequencing — them, or your need for a predictable response?

2. If 连结式关系 ("非审计付出") and 商业算盘与激励 ("先看清激励结构") are both true, what specific signal tells you which frame you're in before you've already committed?

3. The "高度自主性的价值共创模式" hypothesis has sat unoperationalized since the profile compile. What would it take to falsify it — and have you tried?

4. Your pipeline principle (知识系统与自我维基) optimizes for "可重复合成". Which of your six L2 principles has actually been stress-tested through repeated synthesis vs. merely authored once?

5. The red-link graveyard (2015–2017 diaries, philosophy, learning) represents a self you no longer distill. If that earlier self contradicts your current principles, would the pipeline even surface it — or does "复利 distillation" silently compound only what you already believe?

title: autonomy
excerpt: [AI Synthesis]: Autonomy is living with restored awareness, spontaneity, and intimacy—present-moment candor free from compulsive games. It requires a friendly divorce from parental and cultural scrip…
excerpt_search: [AI Synthesis]: Autonomy is living with restored awareness, spontaneity, and intimacy—present-moment candor free from compulsive games. It requires a friendly divorce from parental and cultural scrip…
body:
[AI Synthesis]: Autonomy is living with restored awareness, spontaneity, and intimacy—present-moment candor free from compulsive games. It requires a friendly divorce from parental and cultural scripts, even at social cost, and a continual fight against sliding back.

The three capacities
 Autonomy shows up as the expression or recovery of three abilities: awareness, spontaneity, and intimacy.
 Beyond filling time until death or Santa Claus, awareness transcends classification, spontaneity rises above past programming, and intimacy is more rewarding than games—yet all three can frighten the unprepared.
 There may be little hope for the human race as a whole, but there is hope for individual members of it.

Awareness
 Awareness requires being here and now—seeing and hearing in one's own way, not only the way one was taught (the jay/sparrow lesson).
 The aware person is alive because he knows how he feels, where he is, and when it is; he knows that after he dies the trees will still be there but he will not be there to look at them again, so he wants to see them now with as much poignancy as possible.
 He is living in the present moment with the environment that is here—the sky and the trees as well as the feeling of motion.

Spontaneity
 Freedom to choose and to express Parent, Adult, and Child feelings in varied ways.
 Liberation from the compulsion to play games and from having only the feelings one was taught to have.
 Liberation of one's own native feelings, no longer steered by others' prescriptions.

Intimacy
 An aware person's spontaneous, game-free candidness—eidetic perception freed, innocence of an uncontaminated Child ego state, living in the here and now.
 Intuitive perception evokes affection; candor mobilizes positive feeling.
 They encourage the other person to speak freely by inviting direct eye contact.
 Intimacy is essentially a function of the natural Child; without game interference the outcome tends to be positive—most infants seem loving.
 Intimacy degrades when adapted to Parental influence.

Path to autonomy
 Exclude the grip of tribe or family tradition.
 Discard influences from parents, society, and culture—fully reckon with modern social demands.
 Gain personal and social control so behavior classes become free choices under one's will.
 Accept partial or total sacrifice of benefits from one's current social circle.
 Give up the easy rewards of being a Sulk or a Jerk.
 Essence: a friendly divorce from one's parents (and other Parental influences)—they may be visited agreeably, but no longer dominate.
 Overthrow is never final; there is a continual battle against sinking back into the old ways.

Actions
 Once a day, pause to name feeling, place, and time before acting—train Adult awareness of the present environment.
 When an exchange feels scripted, choose one spontaneous, game-free response (a direct feeling or question) instead of the usual move.
 Practice seeing without immediate labeling—notice the thing before the Parent name for it.
 Expect social cost when dropping a game circle; plan which benefits you are willing to sacrifice.

body:
log of trainings & books and my ratings

reading-2026

- [How to Live an Extraordinary Life] by Anthony Pompliano (8/10)
- [When Love Meets Fear: Becoming Defense-less and Resource-full] by David Richo (8/10)
- [The psy of leadership] by Sébastien Page (9/10)
- [Awareness: The Key to Living in Balance] by Osho (7/10 note: ethical codes are useful for society, but not useful for individual)
- [Difficult Conversations: How to Discuss What Matters Most] by Douglas Stone, Bruce Patton, Sheila Heen (8/10)
- [Antifragile: Things That Gain From Disorder] by Nassim Nicholas Taleb (8/10)
- [財富自由心理學] by 蔡宇哲, 郝旭烈 (8/10)
- 做一個情緒自由的人 by 盧文建, 彭振桓 (6/10)
- 成為自由人 by 李惠貞 （9/10）
- [活出你的本來面目] (8/10)  
- [The Psychology of Money] by Morgan Housel (9/10)  
- [The four agreements - a Practical Guide to Personal Freedom] by Don Miguel Ruiz (8/10)

- [The Power of Charm] (8/10)  
- [The Daily Stoic] by Ryan Holiday

Build myself - healthy, free, wealthy, and loved  
 > always be kind to yourself  
    > - treat yourself as your dear friend, with kindness and patience  

 > you only can "Make" yourself, not "Found" youself  
    > - keep learning, thinking & risking  

 > Ready is an illusion. No one is ever ready.
    > - We just get less unprepared. Never prepared.  
    > - Fake it and then make it  

 > start with your vision and deal with reality
    > - not what is possible and  then decide what result you want to create

 > keep healthy and fit
    > - avoid injuries 
    > - keep rest 
    > - exercise 

 > build a clear & calm & peace of mind  
    - know your own mind - how your mind works 
        + need insight into your own thinking process 
        + write the diary 
        + don't shrink from challenges which could provide growth 


    - be true to your deepest and most profoundly felt emotions   
        + those of a spiritual nature
        + not the surface level emotions of fleeting hormones
        +  ground yourself in wisdom, self-honesty, principles and discipline

    -  attain peace with your mind - self awareness
        + their mind is humble servant and not a terrible master
        + the less judgemental you are,
            - how your mind works, and how to attain peace
        +  Mere observing, rather than making conclusions of the situation

    - a few basic emotions: joy, trust, fear, surprise, sadness, disgust, anger and anticipation

    - happiness is about peace, all you want is privacy, not to be famouss

    - growth happens in the places you're scared to go


Build love and families 
 kind, cheerful, understanding, graceful, independent

 close friends, value quantitys more than quality 
    - they know who you are, not what you are 
    - get around like minded positive people 
    - form trustworthy, deep bonds, fewer the better

learn about yourself    
 time and peace of mind are the most expensive mode of payment

       >  + 交流进而产生对比,对比自然分出高低; 低的自然模仿高的

 just being yourself is the biggest favor you can do to yourself
    -  people may or maynot help you depending if you are falling in their story line
    -  they first like you and then to feel good they help you
    -  people help you because they like you, people don't help you because you are smart
    -  forget about sounding smart, just be yourself


 learn about yourself and grow by put yourself into unfamiliar situations
    -  see how you respond to them to adapt
    -  travellings can put you in lots of novel situations to accelerate growth


 expressing yourself is more important than impressing others.
    -  one must not seek recognition from others

        +  people remember the impact you have one them. Impression is ephemeral  


 focus on people who share your values right from the beginning , not everyone
      

 how to morality

    -  prey on or look for ways to hurt people

Build love and families  
 尊重和确认的力量  - 对伴侣观点的关心和尊重
    -  行为描述  
      > + 在精确表述上表现很糟糕, 如果抱怨某事,同时谈及几个问题
      > + 彼此倾听方面表现糟糕, 很少耐心自习思索伴侣所说的话 
      > + 尽可能清楚明白, 详细具体地指出惹恼我们的特定行为, 应该专指某一特定事件, 不涉及普遍性
        > - 用第一人称明确说明自己的感受 “当你在x情景下做x的时候,我感到z”
      > + 复述和向对方检验自己的知觉, 积极主动地努力理解自己的伴侣

  Never let resentment set in  
    - resolve things quickly  
    - cultivate a culture of honest & loyalty  
    - appreciate and gratitude her  


Strategies on relationships  
 be open-minded    
    - you're curious about how things work, why people think what they think, and are willing to listen  
    - it doesn't mean you have to accept or tolerate anything you don't agree with  

 > Don't show kindness to people who want to destroy you
    > - your kindness will be forgotten and they will not do the same for you
    > - don't be kind towards harmful personss  

  don't waste time explaining yourself to people who don't like you

 focus on people who can take care of themselves
    - the secret of effortless relationships


  only real friends want you to be happy, or end it.
    - a friend is the one that crafts you for a better person, not a worse one

  don't disagree unless you have to, and agree when you can  


HOW to communicate well     
 stragegy
    - Always give before you take
        + soften the ground, take the bit out of a future request, or simply create a distraction
        + like an actual gift, a generous act, a kind favor, an "honest" adminssion
    - 做人有底线就够了, 不要追求风骨, 身段, 没有用处  
    -  一个人不断进步的结果是遇到越来越精彩和优秀的人，你知道他／她真的很优秀，从外在到内心  

    - 如果你想要说服别人，要诉诸利益，而非诉诸理性


 > 工作中的沟通  - 沟通是为了让进度顺利推行, 更容易做事  
    > - 对上 -> 取得信任与默契
      > + 先听懂对方说的话, 别急着表现自己的立场与想法
      > + 培养彼此默契, 了解双方的差异
      > + 懂得询问公司的目标与主观的想法, 再加入适当的个人建议,并再次询问主管对你提出的意见有何想法
      >     - 让主管明白你不只是听懂他的话, 而且还能抓到重点, 并且顾及不同层面并提出适当建议
      > + 循序渐进地让主管慢慢和你站在同一阵线  

    > - 对下
      > + 交代工作清楚, 确保对方明白 -> 该做的准备, 以及应达成的任务
      > + 也要让对方有发表意见的反馈机会 -> 让工作朝彼此目标共同前进, 还能理解他人的想法

    > - 同事 - 尊重
      > + 沟通 - 站在对方的立场思考, 这样容易达成共识


 商业伙伴的沟通
    - 学会尊重商业伙伴和博弈对手
        + 改掉那种沾别人点便宜就觉得别人傻的恶习, 否则, 路越走越窄
        + 别人一时不在乎并不意味着别人傻 - 他们比你聪明的多

    - > win-win  
      > + 求同存异 - 共赢 + 不失原则的妥协
          > - 共同的，不同的和处于中间带的观点  
      > + 风险共担, 利益共享的模式  
      > + 该讲法律的地方不要强调道德  

    - 沟通的关键是找出差异与共同点； 信任是 了解对方的核心诉求，极力维持
        + 不是让对方全盘接受, 而是找出彼此的差异与共同点  
        + 协调出大家可以相互配合,折中的方式  

 社交能力  
    - > 知道怎么站在别人的角度思考问题  
      > + 尝试理解对方的需求；人际关系的本质是 了解和应对别人的需求  
      > + 外交的艺术就是把你的愿望变成别人的愿望  

    - > 演技/掩饰 - 改变口音  
      > + 没有信心时， 佯装自信  
      > + 一旦获得成功，假装害羞和自我怀疑，以免引发他人妒恨  

    - 有一个高质量的朋友圈（价值观一致，有一些相同的爱好，在一起说话，最好有趣一些）

 peaceful of minded 
    - meditation 
    - diary  

 experience
    - nature
    - exercise
    - chatting

body: #business #startup 讲道理，讲故事，讲实在的事情 观察 和聊 员工想要的是什么 直接讲 心里想要的是什么 自己的定位， 和员工的自己的定位 确认他的意愿，然后培训， 和工作上相应的安排 由上而下： 资源+环境，coaching 让大家有参与感 学习型组织： - 试点：读书会， 引进外部的教练 - 参加后 互动讨论 - 复制出去 加工资： - 列出自己的战绩/数据 -最近工作的进展/成果， 这些技能， 然后可以用这些为公司做 - 然后 提议 加薪 如果我想做到下一个职位， 问下老板，我还需要做些什么 - 和老板对焦， 目标更明确， 和专注 - 让老板知道这个意愿 Polite Team work Question why - critical thinking Active 销售 - 对自己的了解： 声音，人格，举止 - 是给别人带来 value - 了解自己的产品， 自己的优势和劣势； - 了解对方， 建立互信基础 销售， 要听清楚 别人的问题 找到决策的关键人物 满足客户 先投资，后销售 帮助客户的决策

body:
[AI Synthesis]: Charm is a learned social skill: make people open and receptive by raising their sense of being valued. Self-esteem sits at the core; people decide emotionally first, then justify logically.

What charm does
 Business and personal life hinge on communicating effectively — social intelligence: interact, converse, negotiate, persuade.
 Charm makes others open and receptive to your message — more willing to be influenced.
 Decide today to develop the power of charm and practice it.
 Charm can be learned.

Self-esteem and feeling valued
 The core of personality is self-esteem — how much you like yourself; the sum of how important and valuable you feel at any moment.
 Human beings are intensely emotional: they make decisions emotionally, then justify them logically.
 The need to feel valued and valuable → make others feel important.
 Acceptance; you smile; they like the person who is making them feel this way — they feel important and valuable.
 Attention.

Actions
 Observe how charming people behave; use what you learn.
 Smile with happiness at seeing people.
 Say “thank you” on every occasion, large or small.
 Praise people for what they have done; compliment a trait, possession, or accomplishment.

body:
[AI Synthesis]: Charm a woman by being captivated by her as a person: affection, attention, respect; questions about her life; quiet attentive listening; courtesy; find something to be impressed by.

Emotional connection
 Caring and concern, plus confidence and competence in the world.
 Be totally captivated by her as a person and by every word she says.
 Ask about herself, her day, life, concerns, hopes, background, goals; listen quietly and attentively.
 Genuine concern for her feelings and experience creates a powerful bond.
 Be drawn by her ideas, opinions, character, and personality.

Actions
 Offer affection, attention, and respect.
 Talk and listen as if she is the most fascinating person you ever met.
 Extreme courtesy and respect; ask questions and listen closely.
 Acceptance, appreciation, and approval — ask about work and personal life; find something to be impressed or amazed by.

body: #china #self 开会， 让我们投资，赚大钱 传销 - 多层次直销， 一种人传人的方式来达到销售的市场策略 - 以会员制的方式，直接或间接发展人员的销售业绩为依据计算报酬 - 如果机构收入来源主要是 产品或服务的销售，对参与者的奖励主要基于对产品或服务的推销工作，则合法 如果机构的收入来源主要是来自于 新参与者所缴纳的钱款，对参与者的奖励主要基于吸纳新参与者的工作的话，以及使用限制 人身自由的方式，则非法 - 收入纯碎来自 新参与者的“入会费” - 也可能是 所销售的产品实际价值很低，但对新参与者供货的“批发价”很高 - 或者 新参与者付出很高的 入会费，所获仅仅很低价值的产品 - 销售奖金的方式 主要来自介绍他人加入的“入会费” 什么是成功 - 速成， 暴富理论 <- 过于被 结果 牵引 自我抑制的伪君子， 就比真小人要好 在一个弱肉强食的世界里， 做君子没有什么好处 “明枪易躲暗箭难防”， 那是对强者而言 做奴隶的国度， 失去了自我， 老是从 主人的角度看问题 #self #life #important 每个人的生命都是以自我为中心的， 这一点与道德无关 - 毫不利己专门利人，只不过是一个道德理想状态 - 较好的人能做到 利己也利人 - 一般人只能做到 不害人而已 快乐是稀少的， 只存在于 美于爱之中 - 看到 美景 - 爱上某个人的一瞬， 被某人所爱的一瞬 - 为一本小说/电影 感动的一瞬 - 要想获得肉体的舒适和精神的愉悦，机会不多 #life #important 清醒的生活 - consciousness 对生命真正的享用 - 过 经过考量的生活 - 用心地刻意地对快乐的追求 才是对生命的享用 - 用心计划如何花费自己的时间 - 只做自己最喜欢做的事情 - 不要随波追流，按照 生存的本能去做不得不做的事情， 懵懂地消耗掉生命 - 不要用 忙碌 来忘却存在 激情 是生命力的表现 - 对于自己的生命力，要让它充分表达， 充分实现 - 有什么冲动就去做什么， 冲到到什么程度就做到什么程度， 不强求，不压抑 - 要想一下 是不是自己发自内心的冲动， 是否为自己带来快乐和满足的感觉即可 - - 如果你有激情去做某一件事，就去做， 不必刻意压制 - 如果你有激情去追求一种关系比如恋爱，朋友， 就去做 - 激情是人生的困扰，应当在适当的时候放弃激情 宁静是至关重要的 - 宁静是幸福的基础 - 平静 是 激情的对立物 - 安静的力量是沉着的，比起噪音，它更接近真实 - 更有力量，因为真理在握或者 真相在握 - 对自己的观点有信心，因而有底气，有力量，不畏惧攻击和辩论

> Effective communication specifies behavior, uses I-statements, and validates the partner's viewpoint. Poor listening and vague grievances erode intimacy.

Core patterns

- Conflict: one issue at a time; avoid generalizations; seek understanding before fixing.
- Overlaps 先利益后逻辑: validation before logic; 连结式关系: feel understood first.

IIMBx 创业与营销管理笔记：人们买的是利益与感受；营销从消费者出发，销售从厂商出发。人员管理强调角色目的、通过他人成事、诚信与委派。 - 消费者决策：需求缺口→信息搜索→评估替代→购买→购后。 - 差异化、竞争、定位：在消费者心智中占有利位置；价值主张；定位动态。 - 细分与目标市场；商业模式 = 价值创造活动。 - 明确角色对组织与职业的贡献与目的。 - 信任决定委派；享受下属成功；以身作则的诚信（镜像测试）。 - 发展空间：试点项目、非结构化任务、转机、跨职能团队。 - 误解→防御→不信任→冲突；主动倾听（听懂未说出的）。 (Source: raw/posts/course/2023-03-20-entrepreneurship.md)

Distillation (2026-06-16) - source: raw/posts/diary/2023-09-04-the-log-of-your-life.md
延续「人生日志」框架，本卷覆盖 2023-09-04 至 2023-12-27 的 TODO/REVIEW 周记。 [AI Synthesis] 与 2022 卷相比，重心从政治社会观察转向现金流思维、创业书单、亲密关系沟通与「灵魂 vs 小我」的内在工作。 - 追踪重要行为的频率、时长与情境；结构化反思 + 未来预演。 - 决策日志：日期、人/项目、决策或反馈、结果。 - 连接：对内了解情感，对外共振；少理论多实战，大问题拆分。 - 自信：问 how 不问 why；关注「我有什么」「我可以学什么」；积极看待能力与机会，勿自我限制。 - 不要把希望寄托在别人身上；调节情绪，直面觉得重要的事。 - 让人信任而非让人喜欢；自我表达很重要。 - 金钱只强化现有的自己；用现金流（稳定持续收支）替代单纯盯账户。 (Source: raw/posts/diary/2023-09-04-the-log-of-your-life.md)

Distillation (2026-06-16) - source: raw/posts/diary/2025-07-10-notes-odyssey.md
本卷为「奥德赛」式自我探索日志（2025-07-10 → 2026-02-06），非周复盘结构。主轴：Study the self → forget the self；自由灵魂、自我接纳与真实连接。 [AI Synthesis] 相较 2024 人生日志，本卷更深地进入荣格式阴影/个体化、NVC 与 assertiveness、讨好→一致型转化。 - 对象：Free Spirit、理解自己、真实连接；believe → attitude → behavior → resist。 - 实践线：冥想、专注呼吸、主动倾听、萨提尔觉察；阅读 Untethered Soul、力量从哪里来、Making of Manager 等。 - 最大抗拒：钱/自由/懒、灵魂与身体的死亡；坟场、赌场等体验式任务。 - 自主：主动编写剧本；成熟自主 = 有边界的信任，非独自扛一切。 - 尊严：我是完整的人，不是工具；抗拒金钱逻辑控制关系。 - 真实亲密：脆弱与理解并存；欲望是连接力量，愤怒是守门人。 - 完整：接纳光明与阴影 → 内在平和；底线一致（善良、尊重、自主），表达可分层。 (Source: raw/posts/diary/2025-07-10-notes-odyssey.md)
